comparison_intro: The same five non-halfway values round to the same integers. These translations calculate a result column while retaining the input values.

language_notes.sas: ROUND uses unit 1 by default. The macro reads a SAS dataset and writes a new one. SAS harness is supplied but unexecuted.
language_notes.python: pandas Series.round(0) computes nearest integers on a copied DataFrame. Numeric displays such as 2 and 2.0 are equivalent here.
language_notes.r: Base R round(value, 0) returns numeric results. Its halfway behavior must not be generalized to SAS ROUND.

semantic_notes.title: Keep the scope explicit
semantic_notes.text: The original five values and the added integer-boundary probes exclude halfway cases. Other units and SAS floating-point adjustments are outside scope.

semantic_notes.title: Output and explanation differ
semantic_notes.text: Matching results on these rows do not prove all ROUND implementations equivalent. pandas and R use ties-to-even; SAS documents a different exact-tie rule.

tests.name: Original fixture: known answers
tests.catches: Wrong direction, truncation, missed negative values or hard-coded mismatched outputs.

tests.name: Added probes around integers
tests.catches: Floor, ceiling or truncation substituted for nearest-integer rounding.

tests.name: Preserve inputs, types and order
tests.input: All CSV rows in reverse order, with custom row identifiers.
tests.expected: Fresh result; source values unchanged; original order retained; rounded numeric; reordered expected values match.
tests.catches: Input mutation, sorting, result text instead of numbers, or position-dependent/hard-coded answers.

scope: Nearest-integer rounding for the original five finite, non-halfway values plus explicit non-halfway validation probes. Exact/near-halfway cases, other units and general SAS equivalence remain excluded.
